status: Written from §8 and §9 for review: a Level III confirms each case's expected grade (and the boundary readings: 'exceed', 'greater than', 'inclusive') before the table is relied on.

clauses.8.0: B31.1: Discontinuities that produce an indication greater than 20% of the reference level shall be investigated ... (1) cracks, lack of fusion or incomplete penetration are unacceptable regardless of length. (2) Other discontinuities are unacceptable if the indications exceed the reference level amplitude and have lengths exceeding: 0.25 in for T up to 0.75 in inclusive; T/3 for T from 0.75 in to 2.25 in inclusive; 0.75 in for T over 2.25 in.
clauses.9.0: B31.3: A discontinuity is unacceptable if the amplitude of the indication exceeds the reference level and its length exceeds: 0.25 in for T up to 0.75 in; T/3 for T from 0.75 in to 2.25 in; 0.75 in for T over 2.25 in.
clauses.7.4.2.1(4): For flaws exhibiting indication amplitudes greater than the instrument saturation level, the flaw length shall be the distance between the flaw ends that equal the reference level (80% screen height).
